previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain similar to prior angina, found to be due to hypertensive emergency and underlying coronary artery disease. Initial presentation included elevated blood pressure, ST depressions on EKG, and a rise in troponin, consistent with intermediate coronary syndrome. Contrast-induced nephropathy occurred after CT imaging, complicating management and delaying planned cardiac catheterization. The patient also experienced neck pain with muscle spasms, constipation, and required medication adjustments due to an aspirin allergy and renal impairment. Blood pressure was stabilized with amlodipine and hydralazine, and lisinopril was held. A stress test revealed a reversible lateral defect, indicating ischemia. The patient was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient follow-up, aspirin desensitization, and future reevaluation for revascularization once renal function improves.
